newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt surges on Mexico election, strong T-bond.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt surges on Mexico election, strong T-bond.

text.p: The Mexican elections boosted emerging debt prices on Monday, as investor interest and dealer trade sent the market to record highs, Brady bond traders said.

News of stable and fair elections in Mexico brought investors from the sidelines, even as Mexicans handed the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) its first loss of a Congressional majority since 1929.
"There's a lot of euphoria after these elections," said Walter Molano, director of Latin American research at SBC Warburg. "That drove the market early in the morning, bolstered by the long bond."
The Brady bond rally was aided by a surging U.S. bond market, where the benchmark U.S. T-bond climbed 20/32 to yield 6.58 percent.
Mexico's global bond due 2026 MXUMS=RR soared 1-1/4 points to 118, while its par bonds MX625L19=RR rose 5/8 to 80-1/8.
"It's a real step in the right direction towards plurality and a more democratic structure and that's positive," one Brady bond dealer said.

Mexicans voted for change, handing the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) its first loss of a Congressional majority since 1929. Also, veteran leftist candidate Cuauhtmoc Cardenas captured Mexico City mayoral race.
"There's definitely relief that the Mexican elections are past," said Dan Peirce, chief strategist at Bank of Boston."

"Not that anyone was scared about the results, but people may have kept some ammunition aside hoping for a dip after the elections. Now that the elections are past, they didn't get that dip, and still have to buy," Peirce said

"There's a lot of cash out there and it has been generally underinvested," another Brady bond trader said. "We saw some client flows, but not to warrant this kind of move. I think there are still more dealers than clients."
Argentine paper surged on comments by Economy Minister Roque Fernandez that Argentina would consider buying back some of its Brady bonds.
Argentine FRBs ARFLC05=RR rose 1/4 to 94-3/4, while the country's Pars AR4C23=RR gained 5/8 to 72-1/4.
